{"passages":[{"reference":"20.16","text":"And the father said, “I sinned; I confess it.” Annoubion said, “I too, together with him, ask you to forgive a noble and good old man who was deceived, for the unfortunate man has become the plaything of the notorious fellow. But I will tell you how it happened. This good old man came to greet us. At that very hour, all of us who were present there happened to be listening to Simon, who wanted to run away that night because he had heard that certain people were coming from somewhere, here to Laodicea, under a royal order to search for him. When Faustus came in, Simon stated his own intention and spoke to us as follows: ‘Halōn him when he comes, and make him partake with you. I will prepare an ointment so that, after he has dined, taken it, and anointed his own face, he may appear to everyone to have my form. But you will first be anointed by me with the juices of a certain plant, so you will not be deceived by his unfamiliar form; to everyone else, however, Faustus will appear to be Simon.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"παίγνιον γὰρ γέγονεν ὁ δυστυχὴς τοῦ περιβοήτου","chosen":"the unfortunate man has become the plaything of the notorious fellow","rationale":"Preserves the image of Faustus as a plaything and the substantival force of περιβόητος without supplying Simon’s name."},{"source_quote":"ἀκηκοὼς ἐπιδημήσειν ποθέν τινας ἐνταῦθα τῇ Λαοδικείᾳ","chosen":"because he had heard that certain people were coming from somewhere, here to Laodicea","rationale":"ποθέν means “from somewhere”; ἐνταῦθα and the dative name identify Laodicea as the destination or present location."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἴδιον θυμὸν φήσας","chosen":"stated his own intention","rationale":"θυμός can denote one’s inward purpose or disposition here; “anger” is possible lexically but does not fit the ensuing disclosure as well."},{"source_quote":"μύρον τι","chosen":"an ointment","rationale":"μύρον denotes a perfumed oil or ointment; the following anointing favors “ointment.”"},{"source_quote":"τῆς ξένης αὐτοῦ μορφῆς","chosen":"his unfamiliar form","rationale":"ξένος here describes the form as foreign or unfamiliar to the observers, not necessarily as belonging to a literal stranger."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"Ἁλῶν αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα συμμετασχεῖν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε","issue":"The printed Ἁλῶν does not yield a defensible construction with αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα and ποιήσατε. It has therefore been transliterated rather than silently replaced in the translation. The context appears to call for an instruction to take or secure Faustus when he arrives, but that sense is not supported by the printed form itself.","proposed_reading":"ἑλόντες αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα συμμετασχεῖν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"20.17","text":"While he was proposing these things, I said, “What benefit is there for you now in such a scheme?” Simon said, “First, those searching for me will arrest him and stop their search against me. And if he should even be killed by the royal hand, his children—who abandoned me, took refuge......... and are assisting—will experience the greatest grief.”

“For now, Peter, I confess the truth to you: I was afraid of the .........stō to disclose this. But Simon did not even give us time to confer privately..........mōn; to him Simon’s evil counsel appeared. Nevertheless, in the middle of the night Simon got up and fled toward Judea, escorted by both Appion and Athenodorus. I then pretended that my body was unwell so that, by remaining behind after they had gone, I might make him return at once to his own people, in case he could escape notice while hiding among you, lest he be seized as Simon by those searching for Simon and die under the royal wrath. I therefore sent him away to you at an untimely hour, and out of concern for him I came by night both to see him and to leave very quickly, before those who had sent....................., having returned.”

Then, looking at us, he said, “I, Annoubion, see your father’s true form, since I was anointed by Simon himself—ōn, as I related beforehand—so that the true form of Faustus might be visible to my eyes. Being utterly astounded, therefore, I marvel at Simon’s magic: although you are standing here, you do not recognize your own father.” As the father, the mother, and we ourselves wept over the misfortune common to us all, Annoubion also shared our grief and shed tears.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ βασιλικῆς χειρὸς ἀναιρεθείη","chosen":"should even be killed by the royal hand","rationale":"Preserves the source’s personifying image of the royal hand rather than reducing it to an abstract governmental authority."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐπὶ Ἰουδαίαν ἐποιεῖτο φυγήν","chosen":"fled toward Judea","rationale":"ἐπί with the accusative marks the direction of Simon’s flight."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τὰ ἑαυτοῦ ἐπανελθεῖν","chosen":"return at once to his own people","rationale":"The idiom may refer to one’s own home, affairs, or people; the following παρ’ ὑμῖν favors Faustus’s family or associates."},{"source_quote":"ἀωρίας","chosen":"at an untimely hour","rationale":"The genitive denotes action at an unusually late or otherwise inconvenient hour."},{"source_quote":"ὅτι ἑστῶτες τὸν ὑμέτερον οὐ γνωρίζετε πατέρα","chosen":"although you are standing here, you do not recognize your own father","rationale":"The participle ἑστῶτες is retained rather than omitted; the concessive relationship is supplied from context."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἵτινες ἐμὲ καταλιπόντες προσφυγόντ......... συνεργοῦσι","issue":"The selected edition prints nine dots after the surviving partial form προσφυγόντ. The unavailable wording and the completion of the participle have not been restored; the same nine-dot gap is retained in English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐφοβούμην τὸν .........στω τοῦτο μηνύειν","issue":"The edition prints nine dots, but the surviving τὸν before the gap and final -στω after it do not form a defensible continuous construction. The ending suggests a dative such as Φαύστῳ, while τὸν is accusative. The translation preserves the mismatch and fragment rather than silently reading “to Faustus.”","proposed_reading":"ἐφοβούμην τῷ [Φαύ]στῳ τοῦτο μηνύειν","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ καιρὸν ἡμῖν ὁ Σίμων ἐδίδου πρὸς τὸ ἰδιάζειν .......... μῶν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ Σίμωνος κακὴν ἐφάνη βουλήν","issue":"Ten printed dots interrupt the sentence and leave the fragment μῶν. Beyond the gap, the accusative phrase τὴν ... κακὴν ... βουλήν cannot straightforwardly serve as the subject of finite ἐφάνη. No defensible continuous English construction can be recovered from the supplied wording, so the fragments are represented without an invented restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"πρὶν τοὺς πέμψαντας ..................... ἐπανελθών","issue":"The selected edition prints twenty-one dots. The missing material prevents secure determination of how τοὺς πέμψαντας and the nominative participle ἐπανελθών were connected. The exact twenty-one-dot gap and the surviving syntactic fragment are retained without restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐναλειψάμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος ὢν προδιηγησάμην","issue":"The nominative participle ὢν does not form a defensible construction with the first-person finite verb προδιηγησάμην in this clause. The context strongly suggests comparative ὡς, “as,” but the translation preserves the printed form as the transliterated fragment “ōn.”","proposed_reading":"ἐναλειψάμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος, ὡς προδιηγησάμην","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"20.18","text":"Then Peter promised us that our father’s form would be restored. He said to him, “You have heard, Faustus, about our circumstances. Therefore, when the deceptive form laid upon you becomes useful to us and you serve us in the matters we command, then I too will restore your true form to you, after you have first done what I tell you.”

The father said, “Anything that is possible for me I will do with the greatest eagerness; only restore my form to my own people.” Peter answered, “You yourself heard with your own ears from my advance messengers, who came from Antioch and said that Simon had been there and had vehemently incited the crowds against me, calling me a magician, a murderer, a deceiver, and a sorcerer—to such an extent that everyone there longs to taste my flesh. You will therefore do as I say: leave Clement with me and precede us to Antioch with your wife and also with your sons Faustinus and Faustinianus. Certain others will accompany you as well, whom I judge capable of serving my purpose.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς μορφῆς τὴν ἀποκατάστασιν","chosen":"that our father’s form would be restored","rationale":"ἀποκατάστασις denotes restoration to the former condition, here explicitly the father’s appearance."},{"source_quote":"ἡ περικειμένη σοι πλάνος μορφὴ","chosen":"the deceptive form laid upon you","rationale":"περίκειμαι depicts the form as something placed around or upon Faustus; πλάνος characterizes it as deceptive."},{"source_quote":"τῶν προόδων μου","chosen":"my advance messengers","rationale":"The substantival plural refers to people sent ahead of Peter; “forerunners” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐμῶν ἀπογεύσασθαι σαρκῶν","chosen":"to taste my flesh","rationale":"Preserves the violent bodily image and the source’s plural σάρκων without replacing it with a generalized desire to kill Peter."},{"source_quote":"προαγαγὼν ἡμᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν","chosen":"precede us to Antioch","rationale":"The following section shows Faustus going ahead and later notifying Peter. Formally, προάγω with an object can also mean “lead us onward,” but that is less consistent with the narrative sequence."},{"source_quote":"ὑπουργῆσαι τῷ ἐμῷ θελήματι","chosen":"serving my purpose","rationale":"θέλημα here is Peter’s intended plan or purpose, while ὑπουργέω denotes rendering practical assistance."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"20.19","text":"“With these people, in Antioch....... while you appear as Simon, publicly proclaim your own change........: ‘I, Simon, proclaim these things to you. I confess that I unjustly spoke falsely........ He is not a deceiver, not a murderer, not a sorcerer, nor is he any of the vile things I formerly managed to say about him while driven by anger. I beg you—I myself became the cause of your hatred toward him—stop hating him. For he is a true apostle of the true prophet sent by God for the salvation of the world. Therefore I myself also advise you to obey him concerning what he proclaims, since your entire city will be utterly destroyed. I want you to know the reason why I have confessed these things to you. During this night, angels of God were severely scourging me, the impious man, because I was an enemy of the herald of truth. Therefore I urge you: even if I myself should come another time, attempt something against Peter, and speak, do not accept me. For I openly confess to you: I am a magician, I am a deceiver, I am a sorcerer. Perhaps it is possible through reorientation to put away the sins previously committed by me.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐν ὅσῳ ὡς Σίμων φαίνῃ","chosen":"while you appear as Simon","rationale":"ἐν ὅσῳ gives the duration during which Faustus visibly bears Simon’s form."},{"source_quote":"οὐ μιαιφόνος","chosen":"not a murderer","rationale":"μιαιφόνος literally evokes blood-pollution or bloodshed and here functions as an accusation of murderous violence."},{"source_quote":"ὅσα ποτὲ φαῦλα περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγων ἔφθανον","chosen":"any of the vile things I formerly managed to say about him","rationale":"φθάνω with the participle conveys having gone ahead or managed to do something; “formerly hastened to say” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ἄγγελοί με τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν ἀσεβῆ ... δεινῶς ἐμαστίγουν","chosen":"angels of God were severely scourging me, the impious man","rationale":"Retains both the appositional accusation τὸν ἀσεβῆ and the continuing force of the imperfect verb."},{"source_quote":"μετανοίᾳ","chosen":"through reorientation","rationale":"The term denotes moral redirection in this context; it is not rendered as mere regret or remorse."},{"source_quote":"ἀπολῦσαι τὰ προπεπραγμένα μοι ἁμαρτήματα","chosen":"to put away the sins previously committed by me","rationale":"ἀπολύω can mean release, dismiss, or put away. The construction leaves some ambiguity between removal of the sins and release from them."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μετὰ τούτων ἐν τῇ Ἀντιοχείᾳ ....... ἐν ὅσῳ","issue":"The selected edition prints seven dots after Ἀντιοχείᾳ. The missing predicate or connective has not been restored, and the same seven-dot gap is retained in English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"δημοσίᾳ κήρυξον τὴν σεαυτοῦ μετα ........ Ἐγὼ Σίμων","issue":"The edition prints eight dots after μετα. Context suggests a word describing Simon’s change or reorientation, possibly μετάνοιαν, but the completion is unavailable and has not been supplied. The eight-dot gap remains explicit.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὁμολογῶ ἀδίκως καταψεύ ........ ἔστι πλάνος","issue":"The edition prints eight dots after the incomplete verbal form καταψεύ. The object and completion of the verb are unavailable; the English preserves both the discernible accusation of speaking falsely and the exact gap without restoring the missing wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.20","text":"As Peter was giving these instructions, the father said, “I know what you want, so do not weary yourself. For when I get there, I will take no less care to say what ought to be said about you.” Peter again instructed him, “When you perceive that the city has changed from its hatred and desires to see us, send word and inform me, and we will catch up with you there. When I arrive there, on that very day I will drive away your alien form and make your own form appear unmistakably to your people and to everyone else.”

After saying this, he arranged for his sons, my brothers, to be with him, and he commanded our mother Mattidia and some of the more loyal people to go with him. But the mother looked reluctantly upon going with him. “For I appear to be an adulteress while consorting with Simon’s form. If I am indeed compelled to go with him, it is impossible for me to recline on the same couch with him. And I do not know whether I can be persuaded even to go with him.”

When she hesitated to leave, Annoubion encouraged her and said, “Believe me and Peter, and also the very voice, that .... is your husband, whom I love no less than you do. And I myself will be with him.........” When Annoubion had said this, the mother promised to go with him.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"διὸ μὴ κάμνε","chosen":"so do not weary yourself","rationale":"κάμνω can mean grow weary or exert oneself laboriously; the father tells Peter that further explanation is unnecessary."},{"source_quote":"τὴν πόλιν μεταβαλομένην τοῦ μίσους","chosen":"the city has changed from its hatred","rationale":"The genitive τοῦ μίσους is taken as the state from which the city turns; “changed in its hatred” is grammatically possible but less suited to the following desire to see Peter."},{"source_quote":"αὐτόθι ἐπικαταληψόμεθά σε","chosen":"we will catch up with you there","rationale":"ἐπικαταλαμβάνω here denotes overtaking or joining Faustus after he has gone ahead."},{"source_quote":"ἀπλανῶς φαίνεσθαι","chosen":"appear unmistakably","rationale":"The adverb means without deception or possibility of mistake, reversing the deceptive appearance imposed by Simon."},{"source_quote":"τῶν γνησιωτέρων τινὰς","chosen":"some of the more loyal people","rationale":"The substantival comparative can describe more genuine, trustworthy, or devoted associates; “loyal” gives the contextual social sense without specifying an absent noun such as “disciples.”"},{"source_quote":"Μοιχὰς γὰρ εἶναι δοκῶ τῇ Σίμωνος συνοῦσα μορφῇ","chosen":"For I appear to be an adulteress while consorting with Simon’s form","rationale":"The mother speaks of how companionship with someone visibly bearing Simon’s form would make her appear; the translation retains μορφή rather than replacing it with Simon himself."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτῆς κλίνης συγκατακλιθήσεσθαι","chosen":"to recline on the same couch with him","rationale":"κλίνη may be a couch or bed; “recline” preserves the literal posture while leaving the marital implication to context."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ φωνῇ ὅτι .... ἐστὶν ὁ σὸς σύμβιος","issue":"The selected edition prints four dots where the subject of ἐστίν would be expected. The context may suggest a demonstrative such as οὗτος, but no restoration has been supplied; the same four-dot gap is retained in English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ αὐτὸς αὐτῷ συμ.........","issue":"The edition preserves only the prefix συμ- before a nine-dot gap. It indicates association or accompaniment, but the particular verb is unavailable. The English gives only the general sense of being with him and retains the exact nine-dot gap.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
